doc.title: Houston Person Part 2 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 2, 1998 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Lincoln Center, Wynton, Faddis and the Swing dance concert
summary: Person praises Lincoln Center's work under Wynton Marsalis and Jon Faddis and describes seeing thousands dance to Illinois Jacquet's band, arguing dancing could bring jazz back.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: Yes. They are sort of interested. But they are going their own way, which is fine with me. But back to Lincoln Center, I think they’re doing a wonderful job there. And especially with the kids programs. And they do as much as they can and they’ve got a forceful guy down there, Wynton, he keeps on fighting. And Jon Faddis, I like what he’s doing too. So there are two guys who are really making big contributions. And they have people who they’re responsible to. But they do what they can, and they do some wonderful things too. They really expose a lot of — really get into more of a concert type thing, which it can be. That’s not what I was talking about earlier. Because Wynton wrote a ballet too. So he’s into dance too. So dance is a very big part of this music.
I think I saw a thing in the New York Times recently that they had done a concert with a dance venue — people were doing the Swing dance out —

Oh Lincoln Center, oh man it was great. I went down to hear Illinois Jacquet’s band. And that’s great. Now I was looking at thousands of people dance. I mean and I was saying to myself, I was talking to Bob Porter and I said, “this is so simple, to really bring jazz back into the mainstream of things. Just let the people dance. Let the people participate.” Because usually what you wind up with is people looking at somebody indulge themselves, and they can’t indulge. It’s like a lot of people have this feeling, you know, you’re on the outside looking in.

And there’s this guy just playing, and you’re looking. Now do you feel like dancing, or clapping even? You can’t. So I can understand people when they say well I’m going over here where I can have some fun. Because that’s where it came from.
